ruby.explanation: RFC 8610 §3.5.4 explicitly accepts optional-key:nonsense without a cut. Ruby commits to the matching key before trying the wildcard.

RFC 8610 §3.6 / Appendix D biguint explicitly uses tag 2. Ruby cddl.rb synthesizes a tag-2 bstr when validating any nonnegative decoded Integer, so it also accepts untagged integer 0. The RFC-derived tag expectation is retained.
Published RFC 8610 §3.8.6 implies .ne. Ruby implements annotation-only .default, as proposed by unverified erratum 9229.

classification.reason: RFC 8610 §3.8.6 gives .default an "implied .ne control"; snug treats .default as an annotation only, as Erratum 9229 (status Reported) proposes and the Ruby reference does (docs/conformance.md S46).

ruby.explanation: RFC 8610 §2.2.3 defines representable value sets. Ruby cddl.rb validates #7.25/26/27 by re-encoding the float and comparing its shortest encoded width exactly; 1.5 therefore fails float32/float64 although representable in both.

ruby.explanation: RFC 8610 §3.5.4 / Appendix A cut disables enclosing choice; Ruby follows D021 branch-local cuts. D301 makes the literal RFC cut snug's default (rule A is cuts:'branch').

classification.reason: snug's deterministic preset is RFC 8949 §4.2.1 plus §4.2.2's choice of one NaN: "If NaN is an allowed value, and there is no intent to support NaN payloads or signaling NaNs, the protocol needs to pick a single representation, typically 0xf97e00." §4.2.1 alone is not offered as a preset; the default valid preset accepts this NaN.
